raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

CSGMV LoRA kernels launch one program per segment and column tile. Inside a CUDA graph the launch grid is fixed at capture, so the current code sizes the segment axis to the whole static metadata buffer. That buffer is sized for the largest captured batch, and every captured graph launches a program for each of its entries, which is unnecessary.

## Modifications

-  Add `csgmv_segment_grid_size` as a helper:
   - Eager launches are unchanged and use the batch's exact segment count
   - A CUDA graph launches `num_tokens // MIN_CHUNK_SIZE + max_loras_per_batch` segment programs, capped at the metadata capacity

## Accuracy Tests

- Added a new regression test
- Checked that related LoRA kernel tests pass

## Speed Tests and Profiling

#### Setup

I benchmarked on 1xH200:

1. Start the server:

```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
    --enable-lora \
    --max-loras-per-batch 8 \
    --lora-paths \
        adapter0=trentmkelly/gpt-4o-distil-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
        adapter1=nvidia/llama-3.1-nemoguard-8b-topic-control \
        adapter2=t83714/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-limo-lora-adapter \
        adapter3=chaeryu/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-summary-ko-100k \
        adapter4=asanchez75/Llama3.1-8b-mcq-lora \
        adapter5=algoprog/fact-generation-llama-3.1-8b-instruct-lora
```

2. Run the benchmark:

```
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang \
    --base-url http://localhost:30000 \
    --dataset-name random \
    --num-prompts 400 \
    --max-concurrency 32 \
    --random-input-len 512 \
    --random-output-len 512 \
    --lora-request-distribution uniform \
    --lora-name \
        adapter0 \
        adapter1 \
        adapter2 \
        adapter3 \
        adapter4 \
        adapter5
```

#### Results

| Metric | `main` | PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Benchmark duration (s) | 49.5 | 38.0 | **−23.3%** |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 2,122 | 2,767 | **+30.4%** |
| Mean E2E latency (ms) | 3,786 | 2,905 | **−23.3%** |
| Median E2E latency (ms) | 3,820 | 2,942 | **−23.0%** |
| P99 E2E latency (ms) | 7,308 | 5,603 | **−23.3%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 14.2 | 10.9 | **−23.3%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 14.3 | 10.9 | **−23.4%** |
| P99 TPOT (ms) | 15.9 | 12.2 | **−23.2%** |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 71.1 | 59.5 | **−16.3%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 45.7 | 33.0 | **−27.9%** |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 438.3 | 429.9 | −1.9% |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+# Smallest csgmv chunk size; --max-lora-chunk-size only changes the largest.

+def csgmv_segment_grid_size(batch_info: LoRABatchInfo, num_tokens: int) -> int:
+    """Number of segment programs a csgmv launch over num_tokens rows needs.
+
+    Under a CUDA graph the grid must cover every batch that replays it, and a
+    smaller batch can use smaller chunks, so assume MIN_CHUNK_SIZE: at most
+    num_tokens // MIN_CHUNK_SIZE segments plus one partial per adapter slot.
+    """
+    if not batch_info.use_cuda_graph:
+        return batch_info.num_segments
+    return min(
+        batch_info.weight_indices.shape[0],
+        num_tokens // MIN_CHUNK_SIZE + batch_info.lora_ranks.shape[0],
+    )
+
